stages.script: Welcome to MeducateMe. Medicine is fascinating, but there is an enormous amount to learn — diseases, symptoms, investigations, treatments, and countless individual facts. There is only so much information we can hold on to if we try to remember everything in isolation. But medicine becomes much easier to understand and remember when we understand the reasons behind disease processes, rather than simply memorising what happens. And this is why I built MeducateMe — to help you make those connections and understand medicine in a more logical way.

MeducateMe is built around three connected ways of learning. One part takes you back to the basics and explains how the body normally works — the physiology and mechanisms that everything else is built on.
Another looks at what changes in disease — what has gone wrong, why it has gone wrong, and how that leads to the symptoms, signs and investigation results we see.

And the third brings everything together through clinical cases, where you can apply that understanding and reason through what is happening in a real patient. My own background is in paediatrics, so the clinical cases you’ll see are mainly based around children. But the physiology, pathophysiology and clinical reasoning behind them apply much more broadly across medicine.

The idea is to move away from isolated facts and towards a connected understanding of medicine — from normal physiology, to disease, to the patient in front of you. I hope MeducateMe helps make medicine clearer, more logical, easier to remember, and more enjoyable to learn.
